_doc: Designated parity-bearing clauses between dogfood docs and their distributed template twins. Each clause stores ONLY markers (anchor + optional pattern), never the clause text — the compared value is read live from the canonical file, so this manifest cannot silently become a stale parallel copy of the clauses it guards (ADR-0050 §1 markers-only discipline). Keep it small and curated: add an entry only for a clause that MUST stay identical across the twin pair. `pattern` (a Python regex) extracts the discriminating value(s) from the canonical section; every captured value must also appear in the twin section. Omit `pattern` to compare the whole normalized section body. Curated §-content clauses (per ADR-0056: the template twin is a derived artifact whose §-content mirror must not silently drift — the class that recurred across PB-0048/0049/0051). Add a clause here whenever a bionic/AGENTS.md §-edit MUST reach the AGENTS.md.tmpl twin; a naive full-section diff is deliberately avoided because the twin diverges by design (ADR tokens stripped, downstream-shaped).

clauses.section: §4 adrs write rules: the Reviews-surface write set — five paths, six writes, the two op kinds, and both rule handles

clauses.section: §4 adrs write rules: the Reviews-surface lifecycle-record table under `## Coverage`, the `report_grammar` frontmatter discriminator, and the filename-date binding the regenerator checks against frontmatter `date`
clauses.pattern: Lifecycle records live in a five-column table under `## Coverage`|source report date, finding id, pass, event, locator|identified by its own header row rather than by its position|so it never merges with the per-goal coverage matrix|A report declares its grammar through the frontmatter key `report_grammar`|whose one recognised value is `lifecycle`|A report carrying no key reads under the frozen legacy counting rule|a report dated after 2026-09-08 carrying no key is refused|an unrecognised value is refused; neither is defaulted|That date is the report's filename date, which the regenerator checks against the frontmatter

clauses.section: §4 adrs write rules: the reviews index splits raised from standing, and a legacy row carries the literal `unknown`
clauses.pattern: The generated reviews index distinguishes findings raised from current standing|a legacy row carries the literal `unknown` as a positive value|never blank, never omitted, never `0`, and never recomputed from later records|A legacy row that raised nothing renders the bare literal `unknown` with no count|its `raised` cell reads `0 \(legacy\)`

clauses.section: §4 adrs write rules: the Reviews-surface assessment table under Coverage — seven columns, availability/alignment as two fields, the per-goal alignment rollup, and the measured_objectives measurement outcome
clauses.pattern: The Coverage section additionally carries a seven-column assessment table|one row per measure part, identified by its own header row and never by its position|seven columns keeps it disjoint from the five-column summary table and the five-column lifecycle record table|so no two of the three tables are confusable and a mistyped header cannot silently reassign rows|are two fields, never one|six of the sixteen pairs are legal and the rest are refused|The per-goal matrix survives beside the assessment table and carries the derived alignment rollup|a goal no part attempted, including one that yields no parts, is `not-assessed`|carries one entry per COUNTED THING|`measured` and `attempted` both discharge the three-report rotation|`not-assessed` and `unknown` discharge nothing|A report carrying no `measured_objectives` key reads as the literal `unknown` for every goal|A report carrying a flat list of bare ids demotes to `attempted` and is never promoted|a finding whose confidence is `unresolved` is never routed to Revoke|Revocation requires positive evidence that continued observance produces a named cost against a named objective|dormancy, a missing run binding and unavailable evidence are absences and establish none|renders nothing from it, so it adds no row to the regenerative-outputs roster|the objective itself initiates a bounded investigation|every surface a pass read beyond its signal-flagged set is covered by a slip naming it|at most three investigations per pass and five surfaces counted once each per investigation|On the third consecutive `attempted` outcome recorded under this grammar|a demoted entry resets the count and starts no strike|carries one entry per COUNTED THING|every entry carries an identifier of the measure version it concerns|The strongest outcome wins within one counted thing and never across two|a part's count resets only when THAT part discriminates

clauses.section: §11 the assignment contract: the statements survive every hop, only the Outcome narrows, the reviewer is commissioned by the delegator, and the chain terminates at the review, the provenance of a statement, and the boundary against the tool-allowlist rule
clauses.pattern: \*\*The three statements survive every hop\*\*|a forked skill invocation included|Session history carries none of them|The Evidence and the Constraint pass whole|may drop neither|never from the party under review|cannot commission the review of that integration|The chain terminates at the review|never for the transcription that records it|owes the report, not the write|no stop point under the run-autonomy rules|The three statements are authored by the delegator|enters an assignment as quoted data, never as one of the three statements|the tool allowlist remains the sole \*mechanical\* enforcement of separation of duties

clauses.section: §11 the assignment contract: the three dispositions, evidence classified by what it observed, the result token, re-derivation, and the durable record
clauses.pattern: one of three dispositions|\*\*verified\*\*|\*\*contradicted\*\*|\*\*unobserved\*\*|An Evidence item carrying no disposition is a finding|adds no artifact and no field|classified by what it observed, not by the tool that produced it|never raw output, an environment value, or a secret|re-derives each disposition|\*\*The statements land in a durable record\*\*|without the dispatch text or the session

clauses.section: §5.B rule:objectives-read-before-work — every agent reads objectives before work of any size, resolving the tree rather than assuming `docs/`, and re-reads it when it changes
clauses.pattern: \*\*Alignment before work and through delegation\.\*\*|Every agent reads the resolved `<docs_dir>/objectives\.md` before starting work, including small fixes, research, planning, and reviews|Resolve the tree through §14; never assume the literal `docs/` directory exists|Re-read the file when it changes during the work

clauses.section: §5.B rule:orchestrators-read-objectives-at-startup-and-resume — the commander and night gardener read at startup and on resume, the shell-less commander is handed the path, and the gardener's turn gate precedes every read
clauses.pattern: Commander and night gardener read it at startup and on resume|A commander without shell access receives the resolved path from its caller|The gardener's turn gate runs before every other act, reads included|any missing-objectives notice waits for output the gate permits

clauses.section: §5.B rule:objectives-shape-the-work-and-authorize-none — the mission and active goals shape the work under the maturity ladder, a sentence suffices for a small task with no artifact and no approval gate, and objectives authorize nothing further
clauses.pattern: Use the Mission and relevant active goals to assess the task's purpose, tradeoffs, and completion evidence|`exploring` goals remain hypotheses|Do not treat dropped goals as requirements|A sentence suffices for a small task; no extra artifact or approval gate is required|Do not invent a goal association when none is supported|a conflict with an approved plan is a contradicted premise under §11|Objectives alone authorize no additional work

clauses.section: §5.B rule:objectives-context-travels-with-every-delegation — every delegation carries the resolved path plus the mission or an instruction to read it, with known tensions, and session history supplies none of it
clauses.pattern: including a forked skill invocation, carries the resolved objectives path|Include known tensions and require recipients to preserve this context in further delegation|Do not assume session history or a role's installed prompt supplies it

clauses.section: §5.B rule:objectives-populate-gate-never-invents-a-goal — every reader checks the file first, a missing or placeholder file routes to the owner, and no mission or goal is invented to unblock a step
clauses.pattern: \*\*Populate gate\.\*\*|the skill asks the owner to populate it|in an unattended session, write one line naming the gap in the output and skip the dependent step|Never invent a mission or a goal to unblock a step|Apply the populate gate above when objectives are unavailable
